cp.currencyDesc: Base currency, the currencies you trade in, and whether purchase tax counts as cost

currency.subtitle: What money means in this system: the currency the books are kept in, the currencies you can transact in, and how purchase tax is treated.
currency.baseExplain: The currency the books are kept in. Every sales document is in it, every exchange rate is a ratio to it, and every cost and margin figure is expressed in it.
currency.baseLocked: This cannot be changed: {{count}} transaction documents already exist and their amounts were recorded against it. Changing it would not convert anything — it would silently reinterpret every figure in the system. The database refuses it.
currency.baseChangeable: No transaction documents exist yet, so this can still be changed in SQL. Once the first quotation, order, invoice or payment is raised it is fixed for good.
currency.listHint: Turn one on to use it on a purchase order or vendor invoice. Turning one off hides it from new documents; existing documents keep the currency they were raised in.
currency.taxExplain: Off by default. VAT on goods bought for resale is normally recoverable, so putting it in unit cost overstates the cost of goods and understates margin on every line. Turn this on only if your business cannot reclaim it.
currency.taxRetroactive: This applies to goods received from now on. Stock already received keeps the cost it was given at the time.

cp.systemSetupDesc: Currency and costing, countries and phone rules, business identity, tax and fiscal year, document numbering

setup.subtitle: The settings the whole installation depends on: what money means, what a phone number looks like, who this business legally is, and how documents are numbered.
setup.countryNotProvisioned: The country tables have not been created. Apply migration 20260799_system_setup.sql.
setup.defaultCountryHint: Every customer and vendor validates phone numbers against this country unless their own record says otherwise.
setup.defaultCountryCurrency: The currency shown beside each country is the one it trades in.
setup.noCountry: Choose a country to see its rules.
setup.digitsExplain: A mobile here is {{digits}} digits written the way people in this country write it, counting the trunk prefix ({{trunk}}). Whether that prefix is part of the count differs between countries, which is why it is recorded rather than assumed.
setup.areaCodesHint: A landline must start with one of these and carry exactly that area’s number of subscriber digits.
setup.noAreaCodes: No area codes for this country. Landlines here are checked on total length alone — or not at all, if no length is set.
setup.testerHint: Checked against {{country}}. A rule you cannot try is a rule nobody trusts — paste a real number before these start turning customers away.
setup.identityHint: These print on quotations, invoices and purchase orders. They were previously split between branding and the PDF layout, so two documents could disagree. Leave anything that does not apply blank — a blank simply does not print.
setup.legalNameHint: The name on your commercial register, if it differs from your trading name.
setup.taxNumberHint: Leave blank if not registered for VAT.
setup.taxHint: Pre-filled on new sales and purchase document lines, so nobody types 14 forty times a day.
setup.taxNotRetroactive: A default for new lines only. Changing it never alters a line already typed or a document already issued.
setup.fiscalHint: Reports and every “this year” filter currently assume the calendar year and the viewer’s browser timezone.
setup.emailHint: Suggests a correction when an address is a keystroke away from a very common domain — gmai.com, hotmai.com, outlok.com.
setup.emailNoAllowlist: A warning, never a rejection. There is deliberately no list of permitted domains: rejecting an unlisted one would turn away a new customer on their own company domain, which is the worst thing to refuse.
setup.numberingHint: Where each gapless counter stands, and what the next code will be.
setup.numberingEmpty: No counters have been created yet.
setup.numberingNotProvisioned: Apply migration 20260800_document_counters_readable.sql to see the counters.
setup.numberingReadOnly: Read-only on purpose. These counters guarantee that no two documents share a number; a screen that could edit them could break that. Prefixes are fixed in code — changing one would not renumber history, it would start a second series alongside the first.
setup.numberingRestoreWarning: If you ever restore from a backup, these counters must be restored too. Without them numbering restarts at 1 and the next invoice collides with one that already exists.
setup.aiHint: The Knowledge Center can answer questions from your uploaded documents. It reaches the model through an Edge Function so the API key never enters the browser.
setup.aiModelHint: The provider’s exact model identifier, copied from their console. Left blank, the chat says it is not configured rather than failing obscurely.
setup.aiBaseUrlHint: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Leave blank to use the function’s default.
setup.aiKeyBody: NOT here. Anything on this page is readable by every staff member and travels in every backup. Set it on the Edge Function instead:
setup.aiMaxTokensHint: Reasoning models spend this budget thinking before writing. Too small and the answer comes back empty rather than short — 4096 is a safe floor for those, and plenty for ordinary models.
setup.aiModelIsKey: That looks like an API key, not a model name. Keys must never be stored here — every staff member can read this page and it is included in every backup.
setup.aiKeyWhyNotHere: There is deliberately no field for the key on this page. Anything stored here is readable by every staff member and travels in every backup; the function’s secret store is neither.
